source: Written for this app, to fill a gap its own flagship format had: a repo-wide grep for meow, purr, chirp, hiss, yowl or trill returned ZERO hits anywhere in tools/. The cat-story pipeline could describe a cat doing anything except making a sound. NOT AI Video Bootcamp course material - sound_bank.json is the verbatim course transcription and is deliberately left untouched here.
note: Two extra audio layers for the sitcom format, on top of the three sound_bank.json already defines. Every phrase in this file is written to sound_bank's own pattern - <source> <action as an -ing verb> <space or acoustic treatment>, twelve words maximum - and is scored through sound_lint.py like any other prompt. `build_pet_sound.py --check-bank` fails if a single one of them does not. Nothing here duplicates sound_bank: the reset SNAP is composed from that bank's existing `transition` theme ('MOMENTS: something stops, reverses or resets'), which is literally what the reset beat is, rather than a second copy of transition vocabulary living here.

vocal.label: Cat voice
vocal.role: The animal's own voice - the wail, the chirrup, the indignant squeak.
vocal.note: Lands on the character, not the action. If the key effect and the vocal fire on the same frame, move the vocal a few frames earlier - a cat vocalises BEFORE it commits to the move.

snap.label: Reset snap
snap.role: The tiny sound that sells the instant-angel cut.
snap.note: One per episode, on the reset cut and nowhere else. This is the only layer that is allowed to be unrealistic.

hook: small kitten chirruping quietly on a fabric sofa
tiny kitten muttering to itself in a carpeted room
tantrum: tiny kitten wailing indignantly in a carpeted living room
small kitten yowling dramatically across a bright room
tiny kitten mewling in protest on a soft rug
discipline: tiny kitten squeaking in surprise on a soft rug
small kitten chirping sharply beside a wooden table
reset: tiny kitten chirping once brightly in a quiet room
small kitten swallowing a meow in a still room
lecture: small kitten mewling meekly in a quiet living room
tiny kitten trilling apologetically on a fabric sofa

hook: adult cat exhaling slowly through its nose indoors
heavy cat settling onto a fabric sofa cushion
tantrum: adult cat breathing steadily in a quiet room
heavy cat shifting its weight on a woven rug
discipline: low warning chirrup rumbling from an adult cat
adult cat huffing once in a warm room
reset: adult cat sniffing once beside a fabric sofa
heavy cat exhaling sharply in a bright room
lecture: adult cat trilling insistently at close range
adult cat chirruping in short stern bursts indoors
grown cat murmuring steadily beside a small kitten

hook: a human hand resting quietly on a wooden table
tantrum: a human hand tapping impatiently on a wooden table
discipline: a human hand sliding a plastic toy across wood
a human hand lifting a small object off fabric
reset: a human hand withdrawing quietly from a sofa cushion
lecture: a human hand settling onto a woven rug

contact.note: The comedic paw-tap the discipline beat needs. sound_bank's comedy theme has slapstick (n62 'Loud slap like someone smacked a block of cheese') but nothing feline-scaled - these are written to be small.
phrases: soft comedic paw-slap thwack with cartoonish echo
light cartoon bop landing with a comic thud
gentle paw tap thudding softly on fabric

snap_note: Composed from sound_bank.json's own `transition` theme rather than duplicated here. That theme's description is already 'MOMENTS: something stops, reverses or resets' - the instant-angel beat exactly. `snap_prefer` names the four rows of that theme that read as a comic reset (n46 'time resets', n41 'sudden silence', n47 'quick rewind', n49 'clock ticking backwards') and skips the six that are time-travel atmosphere - 'Wind ripping through as the past materializes' is a fine transition and a terrible cat joke. Numbers, not copied text: the phrases still live in exactly one file.
voice_by_beat_note: Which character's voice plays on each beat, by default. The kitten drives hook, tantrum and reset - it is the one performing. The foil drives discipline and lecture, because that is who is doing something on those two: story_bank.json's own must_do for discipline is 'One economical correction from the foil' and for lecture is 'The mother says her piece' - the caption is HER line. Without this mapping, build_pet_sound.extra_layers defaulted every beat to who="lead" because nothing ever overrode it, so the foil's own vocabulary here (the warning chirrup, the stern trilling) was composed but never once reachable from the app.
